transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-25
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Acero ML Eng), Ravi Singh (Acero Platform), Dana Lopez (Acero CTO)

Summary: weekly POC check-in - model selection & pinning. Short review of last week's test and next steps.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh let me kick us off. quick agenda: results recap, select a pin for the pilot, and outline rollback/fallback policies.
[00:12] Maya: thanks Samir, excited to go through. we ran your v2.1 pinned tests last week and saw some interesting stuff.
[00:18] Leah: quick note, the test we sent was host-mode quantized and a fp16 dedicated run; numbers were in the spreadsheet Samir uploaded, if you didn't see it.
[00:28] Ravi: i skimmed it, but big picture: hosted quantized looked cheaper but latency was spiky, dedicated fp16 more consistent but cost jumps.
[00:36] Samir: yeah that's the typical tradeoff; for your 95th pct latency target of ~200ms we were hitting 120-140ms median on dedicated fp16 at 8k context with batching of 16, and hosted quantized was median 160-220ms depending on seq length and cache hit.
[00:54] Dana: those are promising. our SLA for triage is 300ms p95 ideally, but cost is a concern. can you remind us about the cost delta?
[01:05] Samir: sure — rough numbers from the test: hosted quantized ~ $0.12 per 1k tokens in the test profile, dedicated fp16 ~ $0.20 per 1k when amortized over reserved capacity. the Dedicated commitment has a fixed monthly but predictable throughput.
[01:23] Maya: two other things — we saw some hallucination patterns on the older v2.0 model with our prompts, v2.1 reduced that a lot. quantized variant still occasionally truncates or repeats in long contexts.
[01:37] Leah: right, that's why pinning to v2.1 (non-quant) or a verified quantized build might be best. we also recommend a fallback chain: primary pinned model -> quantized compatible variant -> smaller low-cost model as last resort.
[01:52] Ravi: how painful is a rollback if the pinned model degrades? what's the operational steps?
[01:57] Leah: operationally we support canary rollouts and instant pin reassignments via API/console. rollback is basically pin switch and routed traffic, it can be done in under a minute for hosted, dedicated might require rebalancing but still under 5 minutes for routing changes. logs and traces allow you to see regressions.
[02:15] Dana: i want the rollback SLA documented for our procurement team; do you have a template?
[02:20] Samir: yes we'll include rollback/runbook + SLO page in the security pack.
[02:24] Maya: about cache — we tested KV cache and saw token cost drop ~15% and latency improved for repeated prefixes, but cold-starts still expensive.
[02:36] Leah: correct — prefix/KV cache helps when user sessions repeat prompts; for triage flows with similar templates it's impactful. We'll include cache on/off numbers in Leah's tests.
[02:47] Ravi: on the security front, our team asked about KMS integration and audit logs for private deployment, plus SSO/SAML for RBAC.
[02:56] Samir: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SSO; we'll send the SOC2 pack and a KMS integration proposal. we can run Private in a VPC or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[03:10] Dana: good. also question — if we pin a model, can you do A/B pinning for small % to test regressions?
[03:17] Leah: yes, we support percent-based rollouts and A/B; you can route 95/5 to a candidate and run quality evals. our Optimize tool can attach prompt-based evals to flag regressions automatically.
[03:28] Maya: perfect. for the pilot we want to pin to v2.1 but keep a quantized variant as fallback and a smaller 30B as last-resort fallback. is that doable?
[03:36] Leah: absolutely — our recommended chain would be "rw-v2.1-fp16" (primary) -> "rw-v2.1-int8-quant" (fallback1) -> "rw-30b-compat" (fallback2). naming in the catalog might vary, so we'll provide exact catalog IDs.
[03:51] Samir: action: Leah will run pinned v2.1 8k-context tests with KV on/off and include memory/latency/cost., we'll also include a cold-start profile.
[03:59] Maya: one more detail: tokenization differences across model families caused an extra token overhead for our prompts previously, can you confirm token counts used?
[04:06] Leah: we'll normalize using the same tokenizer we used in tests and include tokenization deltas in the sheet.
[04:12] Ravi: on procurement timescales, do we need a PO to start a Dedicated pilot or can we run hosted first?
[04:18] Samir: you can start hosted immediately with usage but if you want Dedicated reserved throughput we'll need a contract (monthly) — we can do a short-term pilot commitment. I'll send options.
[04:27] Dana: please include Dedicated sizing for 3k qps and 10k qps in the doc, ballpark.
[04:33] Samir: noted.
[04:35] Maya: regarding quality gates — can we hook our prompt test suite into Redwood Optimize so we get alerts on regressions?
[04:41] Leah: yes, Optimize supports prompt sets and will send regression alerts and can auto-rollback per policy if you want.
[04:47] Ravi: any competitors we should be aware of in terms of price/perf?
[04:51] Samir: folks do compare with Anthropic and OpenAI managed endpoints; Vertex AI is also mentioned for enterprise infra. We have transparent perf numbers that you'll get in the workbook.
[04:59] Maya: ok next steps recap?
[05:02] Samir: recap: Leah runs the additional pinned tests (8k, KV on/off, cold-start), Samir sends pricing + Dedicated options + SOC2/KMS docs, Maya uploads prompt sets. schedule KMS deep-dive next week.
[05:16] Dana: makes sense, thanks.
[05:18] Samir: any last questions?
[05:20] Maya: nothing else from me.
[05:21] Ravi: all good.
[05:22] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of call.

Notes on transcription quality: minor mis-attributions in a few timestamps and occasional filler words. References to model catalog IDs will be provided in the follow-up sheet.
